QUOTE: "`retryFailedPost`, which rebuilds the API post with `failed: false`, ... then calls `client.createPost` once more." and "On failure, it sets `failed: true` again. The same three error IDs remove the post instead."
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer states retryFailedPost makes one new createPost attempt, and on failure re-marks the post failed or removes it for the same three errors. It does not mention backoff explicitly, but "once more" and "zero automatic retries" cover the no-loop substance.
